title: The accel triad, completed: ENMO-abs (a newly-authored op) bit-for-bit against GGIR

dataset.name: PAMAP2 Physical Activity Monitoring Dataset
dataset.record: subject 101 hand accelerometer (x, y, z in g at 100 Hz), ~62 min free-living (749 epochs of 5 s)
dataset.citation: Reiss A, Stricker D. Introducing a new benchmarked dataset for activity monitoring. 2012 16th International Symposium on Wearable Computers, IEEE, 2012:108-109.

proposition: ENMO truncates the vector-magnitude-minus-1g to zero, discarding any dip below 1 g (deceleration, partial free-fall, or a persistent calibration offset). ENMOa keeps that movement by taking the absolute value instead. The ecosystem had ENMO and MAD (both GGIR-certified) but not ENMOa; this case introduces a NEWLY-AUTHORED op, computeENMOa, completing the accel movement triad. On a real free-living hand-accelerometer recording it reproduces GGIR::g.applymetrics ENMOa to MACHINE PRECISION (max |diff| ~2e-14 g, correlation 1.0) across all 749 epochs; ENMOa >= ENMO at every epoch and exceeds it by ~63 mg on average (mean 224 vs 162 mg) -- the movement below 1 g that ENMO discards.

claims.statement: max |computeENMOa - GGIR g.applymetrics ENMOa| over all epochs (g) -- bit-exact
correlation between computeENMOa and GGIR ENMOa across epochs
number of 5 s epochs certified against GGIR
mean ENMOa across the recording (mg) -- a physical movement-intensity descriptor
ENMOa >= ENMO at every epoch (the abs retains sub-1 g dips ENMO truncates)
mean ENMOa - mean ENMO (mg) -- the sub-1 g movement ENMO discards

validation.reference: The newly-authored computeENMOa op is validated against the field-standard GGIR::g.applymetrics ENMOa on the identical PAMAP2 hand-acc signal (both in g). Both compute the per-epoch mean of |r - 1| with r = sqrt(x^2+y^2+z^2); the agreement is MACHINE PRECISION (max |diff| ~2e-14 g, correlation 1.0) across all 749 epochs. ENMOa >= ENMO at every epoch and exceeds it by ~63 mg on average (mean 224 vs 162 mg).
validation.data: REAL -- PAMAP2 (UCI/PhysioNet), subject 101 hand accelerometer, ~62 min free-living, 749 epochs of 5 s at 100 Hz
validation.note: The reproducible findings are (1) the newly-authored computeENMOa reproduces GGIR::g.applymetrics ENMOa to machine precision (max |diff| ~2e-14 g, correlation 1.0) across all 749 epochs; (2) ENMOa >= ENMO at every epoch, exceeding it by ~63 mg on average. HONEST scope: (1) this op is NEWLY AUTHORED to complete the accel movement triad -- the ecosystem had ENMO (computeENMO) and MAD (computeMAD), both GGIR-certified, but not ENMOa; (2) this is a genuine MACHINE-PRECISION match -- the op and GGIR compute the IDENTICAL per-epoch mean of |r - 1|, so the ~2e-14 residual is the floating-point floor, not a convention agreement; (3) the finding is the ENMO/ENMOa relationship: ENMOa >= ENMO at every epoch (the abs keeps the sub-1 g dips ENMO's truncation discards), and the ~63 mg gap is the movement below 1 g, which matters most when the sensor calibration is imperfect; (4) ENMOa is a physical quantity (g / mg), so the mean is a meaningful movement descriptor, not a reproducibility placeholder; (5) run_simulation = FALSE (deterministic).

open_questions.q: With ENMO, ENMOa and MAD all GGIR-certified, the natural next step is auto-calibration (the GGIR non-wear / sphere-fit calibration that ENMOa is designed to expose): checking whether an ENMOa-vs-ENMO gap flags a calibration offset on uncalibrated data would turn the pair into a data-quality signal. Documented, not escalated.
